key_insight: LLM-generated quantum circuits need layered validation because many failures are structural, not just wrong answers, and can silently contaminate expensive simulation workflows.
engineering_relevance: For quantum software stacks, the paper argues that gatekeeper checks and traceable evaluation infrastructure are essential before LLM outputs are trusted in VQE or materials-informatics pipelines.
method: Seven-criterion gatekeeper screening for physical and framework validity
Circuit fidelity comparison for H2/STO-3G/Jordan-Wigner/UCCSD against analytical/reference values
Run-to-run design entropy to measure behavioral consistency
evidence_signal: Across multiple foundation models in a Materials Project pipeline, the framework identified five failure modes and even found that two apparent model errors were actually caused by the evaluation harness's silent fallback-template substitution.
watch_item: The framework depends on evaluation plumbing being fully auditable, since harness-level substitution or hidden defaults can masquerade as model behavior and undermine conclusions.
paper_title: Gatekeepers and Hallucinations: A Layered Evaluation Framework for LLM-Driven Quantum Circuit Generation
